transcript.text: Sometimes when I open the dishwasher there's grey smelly water in the bottom even though it finished draining fine. Not every day though. Kitchen sink was replaced last month if that matters.

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. From what you have described, the most likely cause is dirty filter / food in the sump. Next: Clean the filter and sump. Let me know what you find.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]

I've already checked the filter and it's clean. Model is a Hotpoint HFC 3C26 W, about 3 years old. The water seems to show up after I drain the sink full of washing-up water. Sink drains a little slow too.
From what you have described, the most likely cause is drain hose / waste plumbing / trap. Next: Check the drain hose/waste and wipe the door seal. Let me know what you find.
I had a look under the sink. Since the new sink went in, the drain hose just lies on the cupboard floor and goes straight into the waste spigot, no high loop in it. Is that the problem?

Very likely, yes. Without a high loop, dirty water from your sink can flow back down the hose into the dishwasher, which fits it happening after you drain a full sink, and the slow-draining new sink makes that backflow more likely. Next: Run a hot maintenance wash with dishwasher cleaner. Let me know what you find.
Ok, I can do the maintenance wash. Should I loop the hose up high under the worktop first and clip it, or just run the wash as it is?

Loop the hose up first. With no high loop, water from the sink, especially after you empty a full bowl, can run back into the dishwasher, so a maintenance wash on its own would likely be undone. Is it a musty/drains smell (a cleaning/maintenance issue) or a burning/electrical smell (in which case stop using it)?
It's a musty smell, like old food water, nothing burning or electrical. I'll loop the hose up and clip it under the worktop, then run the maintenance wash.

Under the sink, look where the drain hose joins the waste. On a newly fitted sink waste the little blanking plug inside the spigot has to be cut out, and the sink trap mustn't be blocked — run the sink tap and check it drains freely. Was the blanking plug still in or the trap blocked (and is it cleared now), or is the connection fine?

I'm not sure about the blanking plug, I couldn't tell you if it was cut out when the sink went in. The sink does still drain a little slow. I've looped the hose up and clipped it now, and there's been no more water in the dishwasher since.
Good news, that has sorted it. If it happens again, start with the same check. Is there anything else I can help with?
